question.problem:
Suppose that $f(x,y)$ is a differentiable function such that

$$
f(2,1)=2,\,{f}_{x}(2,1)=-1,\,{f}_{y}(2,1)=-1.
$$

Using a linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,1),$ estimate the value of $f(1.98,0.94).$
question.worked_solution:
The linear approximation of the function $f$ at the point $(a,b)$ is given by

$$
f(x,y)≈f(a,b)+∇f(a,b)\cdot ⟨x-a,y-b⟩.
$$

So, the linear approximation of $f$ at the point $(2,1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & ≈f(2,1)+∇f(2,1)\cdot ⟨x-2,y-1⟩ \\  & =f(2,1)+⟨{f}_{x}(2,1),{f}_{y}(2,1)⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,y-1⟩ \\  & =2+⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨x-2,y-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

We can approximate $f(1.98,0.94)$ by evaluating the linear approximation at $x=1.98$ and $y=0.94,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1.98,0.94) & ≈2+⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨1.98-2,0.94-1⟩ \\  & =2+⟨-1,-1⟩\cdot ⟨-0.02,-0.06⟩ \\  & =2+(-1)(-0.02)+(-1)(-0.06) \\  & =2+0.02+0.06 \\  & =2.08\end{aligned}
$$
